explanation: The treaty sets the criteria Portugal spent the 1990s meeting: a deficit under three per cent, debt under sixty per cent or falling towards it, inflation and long rates within a margin of the best three, and two years in the exchange rate mechanism. Portugal joined the first group of eleven on 1 January 1999 because it had met them, and meeting them is what Portuguese fiscal policy after 1992 consisted of. The treaty also fixed the shape of the union, with a single monetary policy, no common budget and no lender of last resort for governments. That design let interest rates fall after 1999 with no brake on what the cheap money financed.
